hypotheses.justification: Nothing else in the statement mentions `def_rule`. It is a proof of an equation, so no other part of the statement needs it to elaborate. `applyLocalRule` is defined in LeanPool/PDL/Local/Rules.lean:326 as `| _, ⟨L, R, O⟩ => ress.image (fun (Lnew, Rnew, Onew) => (L \ Lcond ∪ Lnew, R \ Rcond ∪ Rnew, Olf.change O Ocond Onew))`. It ignores its rule argument. So `applyLocalRule rule (L,R,o)` and `applyLocalRule (LocalRule.oneSidedR orule YS_def) (L,R,o)` are definitionally equal for any `rule`. That is already why the statement can pass `hC := hC` to the `LocalRuleApp` field `hC : C = applyLocalRule lr (L,R,O)` with `lr := LocalRule.oneSidedR orule YS_def`. The proof uses `def_rule` in exactly one place: `have c_in' : (L', R', o') ∈ C := hC ▸ def_rule ▸ c_in`. Here `c_in : (L',R',o') ∈ applyLocalRule (LocalRule.oneSidedR orule YS_def) (L,R,o)` comes from `oneSidedR_sat_down` (Rules.lean:402). Because of the definitional equality, this step can be written as `by rw [hC]; exact c_in`, or as `hC ▸ c_in`. That is the same move the proof already makes in the other direction with `(hC ▸ c_in)` when calling `oneSidedR_preserves_left`. The rest of the proof never uses `def_rule`, so the theorem stays true and provable without it.
